## Purpose and input structure

This vignette creates a complete example directly in R. No spreadsheet,
image, saved workspace, or other external data file is required.

The example represents point-quadrat vegetation surveys with **25 measurement
points per transect**. Its column layout, species names, codes, and selected
indicator values follow the example used to illustrate the package's input
format. The survey observations are a small illustrative example, not a full
transcription of the original surveys. The indicator values illustrate data
handling and should not be treated as an authoritative ecological reference.

The combined table contains two kinds of information:

- **Species metadata:** names, unique species codes, Landolt indicator values,
  and the Index of Specific Quality (`ISQ`).
- **Vegetation observations:** survey columns named `R1`, `R2`, and so on.
  Rows represent species; entries are frequency of occurrence (FO).

The following conventions apply to **survey columns**:

- An integer from 1 to 25 is the number of measurement points at which the
  species was recorded.
- `999` identifies an occasional species recorded in the survey area but
  outside the transect measurement points. It is a code, not a frequency.
- `NA` represents an absent species in this example, matching an empty cell
  in the input table. It does not represent an unknown observation here.
- A zero may also be used for absence.

FO is checked per species: the sum across species in a survey need not equal
25, because multiple species can occur at the same measurement point.

## Create the example in R

`data.frame()` creates the required base-R data frame. Character columns are
kept as text and survey columns contain numeric values.

```{r example-data}
example_data <- data.frame(
  species.name = c(
    "Achillea macrophylla",
    "Achillea millefolium aggr.",
    "Achillea moschata",
    "Acinos alpinus",
    "Aconitum lamarckii",
    "Adenostyles alliariae",
    "Agrostis capillaris",
    "Alchemilla vulgaris aggr.",
    "Anthoxanthum alpinum",
    "Arnica montana"
  ),
  species.name.code = c(
    "Achmacr",
    "Achmill",
    "Achmosc",
    "Acialpi",
    "Acolama",
    "Adealli",
    "Agrcapi",
    "Alcvulg",
    "Antalpi",
    "Arnmont"
  ),
  E_Landolt = c(3, 999, 3, 2, 4, 3.5, 2.5, 999, 3, 3.5),
  R_Landolt = c(3, 3, 2, 3, 5, 3, 2, 999, 3, 2),
  N_Landolt = c(4, 999, 2, 2, 4, 4, 2, 999, 2, 2),
  ISQ = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1.5, 1, 0),
  R1 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 999, NA, 5, 999, 6, 999),
  R2 = c(NA, 3, NA, NA, NA, 999, 2, 999, 999, NA),
  R3 = c(1, NA, 999, NA, NA, NA, 1, 4, 999, NA),
  R4 = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, NA, NA, 1, 6, 999, NA),
  R5 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 999, 4, 5, NA),
  R6 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 12, 4, 3, 999),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

n_measurements <- 25L
survey_columns <- grep("^R[0-9]+$", names(example_data), value = TRUE)
```

The pattern `^R[0-9]+$` selects survey names such as `R1` or `R24`, while
excluding the indicator column `R_Landolt`.

```{r metadata-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  example_data[, c(
    "species.name.code",
    "E_Landolt",
    "R_Landolt",
    "N_Landolt",
    "ISQ"
  )],
  caption = "Species metadata (species codes identify the rows)."
)
```

```{r survey-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  example_data[, c("species.name.code", survey_columns)],
  caption = "Survey observations: FO, occasional species (999), and absences (NA)."
)
```

## Check the observations

These checks verify the data-frame class, unique species identifiers, numeric
survey columns, admissible FO values, and the presence of at least one
transect observation in each survey.

```{r validate-input}
stopifnot(
  is.data.frame(example_data),
  !anyNA(example_data$species.name),
  all(nzchar(example_data$species.name)),
  !anyDuplicated(example_data$species.name),
  !anyNA(example_data$species.name.code),
  !anyDuplicated(example_data$species.name.code),
  length(survey_columns) > 0L,
  all(vapply(example_data[survey_columns], is.numeric, logical(1)))
)

fo <- as.matrix(example_data[survey_columns])
observed_fo <- fo[!is.na(fo) & fo != 999]

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(observed_fo)),
  all(observed_fo >= 0 & observed_fo <= n_measurements),
  all(observed_fo == floor(observed_fo)),
  all(colSums(!is.na(fo) & fo != 999 & fo > 0) > 0)
)
```

## Separate the inputs used by the package

The combined table is convenient for data management, but its metadata must
not be interpreted as vegetation observations. For `vegetation_abundance()`,
the **first column must contain species names**, followed only by the numeric
survey columns. Species remain in rows; no transposition is needed.

```{r separate-inputs}
vegetation_data <- example_data[,
  c("species.name", survey_columns),
  drop = FALSE
]

indicator_columns <- c("E_Landolt", "R_Landolt", "N_Landolt")
ecological_data <- example_data[, indicator_columns, drop = FALSE]
isq_data <- example_data[, "ISQ", drop = FALSE]

# Preserve the same species order in all inputs.
rownames(vegetation_data) <- example_data$species.name
rownames(ecological_data) <- example_data$species.name
rownames(isq_data) <- example_data$species.name

stopifnot(
  is.data.frame(vegetation_data),
  identical(rownames(vegetation_data), rownames(ecological_data)),
  identical(rownames(vegetation_data), rownames(isq_data))
)
```

For `ecological_indexes()`, use `vegetation_data` as `database.vegetation`
and `ecological_data` as `database.indexes`. For `pastoral_value()`, use
`isq_data` as the ISQ input and a previously calculated SRA table as the
abundance input. The indicator and ISQ inputs do not include a species-name
column: these functions associate species by **row position**, so keep their
rows aligned even when row names are present.

**The meaning of `999` depends on the input:**

| Input | Meaning of `999` |
|:--|:--|
| Survey observations | Occasional species, not an FO of 999 |
| Ecological indicators | Missing indicator value, using the package convention |
| ISQ input | Missing ISQ value, using the package convention |

An ISQ of **zero is a valid value**, not a missing value. Do not replace `999`
throughout the combined table without first separating these inputs.

## A first calculation

With 25 measurement points, the coefficient for converting FO to percentage
cover is `100 / 25 = 4`. The `SC_fo_occ` method also assigns a percentage
cover of 0.3 to each occasional species.

```{r cover-calculation}
cover_data <- iPastoralist::vegetation_abundance(
  database = vegetation_data,
  method = "SC_fo_occ",
  species.cover.coefficient = 100 / n_measurements
)

knitr::kable(
  cover_data,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Percentage cover, including occasional species."
)
```

The output has species in its row names and surveys in its columns. For
example, the FO of 5 for *Agrostis capillaris* in `R1` becomes 20%, while
the occasional record of *Arnica montana* in `R1` becomes 0.3%.

```{r check-cover, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
  is.data.frame(cover_data),
  cover_data["Agrostis capillaris", "R1"] == 20,
  cover_data["Arnica montana", "R1"] == 0.3,
  cover_data["Achillea macrophylla", "R1"] == 0
)
```

Alternatively, calculate species relative abundance using only transect
observations. With `SRA_fo`, occasional records do not contribute to the
abundance totals.

```{r relative-abundance}
sra_data <- iPastoralist::vegetation_abundance(
  database = vegetation_data,
  method = "SRA_fo"
)

round(colSums(sra_data), 6)
```

Each survey sums to 100% in this SRA table. Percentage cover and relative
abundance are different quantities: percentage cover need not sum to 100%.

```{r check-sra, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(all(abs(colSums(sra_data) - 100) < 1e-8))
```
